summary.title: jq (command-line JSON processor)
summary.one_liner: jq is a lightweight command-line tool for slicing, filtering, mapping and transforming JSON data, written in portable C with no runtime dependencies.
takeaways: jq is a command-line JSON processor meant to be used like sed, awk or grep but for structured JSON data.
It is written in portable C and has zero runtime dependencies, so a single binary can be copied to another machine of the same type.
The official tutorial and manual cover usage in more depth.
Community help is available via the jq tag on Stack Overflow, the #jq channel on Libera.Chat, and a Discord server.
Release history on the page runs from jq 1.3 (2013) to jq 1.8.2 (20 June 2026).
summary.summary: This page is the project homepage for jq, a command-line JSON processor, though the URL redirects to jqlang.github.io. It introduces jq as a tool for filtering, mapping and transforming JSON in the way sed, awk and grep handle text, and notes it is portable C with no runtime dependencies. It points readers to the tutorial and manual, lists community support channels, and gives a dated news log of releases from 1.3 through 1.8.2, including the 1.7.1 security fixes (CVE-2023-50246, CVE-2023-50268).
